data.hook: A post lamenting lost bipartisan dreams hit a nerve, drawing tens of thousands of likes and replies from those feeling the same divide.

data.summary: MOMofDataRepublican shared that both parties once aimed for the same country, just different paths, but no longer believes it true. data.hook: A stark chart from voter data shows Harvard faculty at 99% Democrat, with similar tilts at Yale and Princeton, prompting fresh looks at viewpoint balance in elite universities.
data.name: Chart Reveals 99% Democrats Among Harvard Faculty
data.summary: Researchers Mitchell Langbert and Sean Stevens analyzed 2022 voter registrations, finding Harvard at 99-1 Democrat-Republican, Princeton 98-2, Yale 97-3, and others nearly as lopsided. A Yale report echoed this with 82% Democrats and many departments lacking any Republicans, while Harvard surveys show strong liberal majorities. People debate whether this reflects critical thinking leaning left, indoctrination through hiring biases, or educated folks naturally aligning Democratic, raising questions about diversity in teaching and research.

Voices from veterans, families, and everyday people highlight the personal stakes, while some warn against polls meant to discourage turnout and stress that elections have real consequences.

Critics called them 'human locusts' for fleeing high taxes only to back Democrats again, tapping into debates about California and Washington transplants reshaping Texas politics. While some defend their right to vote, others push for longer residency rules amid steady migration driven by costs and taxes. Early voting tensions highlight how newcomers influence the state's direction.

Hawkish voices argue diplomacy has failed and sustained pressure might topple the regime, while public reactions split on whether voters will reward anti-war positions or see them as weakness ahead of the elections.

data.hook: At packed rallies, Trump painted a stark choice: Republican wins to keep the economy booming, or a 1929-style crash under Democrats.
data.name: Trump Warns of Depression, Pledges $5,000 Payments if GOP Wins Midterms
data.summary: Trump ramped up his midterm pitch with claims of record GDP growth at 3.4 percent in the third quarter, fueled by investment, consumer spending, and government outlays. He warned a Democratic sweep would trigger economic depression and pledged $5,000 to every adult U.S. citizen—costing about $1 trillion from tariffs—if Republicans hold the House and Senate. Polls give Democrats a 70 percent shot at gains on November 3, with reactions split between seeing his words as savvy warnings or early excuses for trouble ahead.

data.hook: With midterms days away, conservative voices are calling out Senate Majority Leader John Thune for not pushing through voter ID legislation despite Republican control of Congress.
data.name: Conservatives Criticize Thune Over Stalled SAVE America Act
data.summary: The SAVE America Act, which requires proof of U.S. citizenship for federal voter registration and photo ID to vote, passed the House but stalled in the Senate. Thune supports the bill but says Republicans lack votes to beat a filibuster without Democrats, and he resists rule changes. Critics accuse him of failing his job amid polls showing 62-83% public support for its elements, while he focuses on campaigning in key states like Maine, Iowa, Ohio, and Alaska. The clash underscores Republican tensions on priorities as Election Day nears.
